subject: maths
title: Pronumerals on both sides and brackets

scenes.heading: Pronumerals on both sides and brackets
scenes.sub: When are two phone plans the same price?
scenes.say: Plan A costs thirty dollars plus five dollars a gigabyte. Plan B costs eighteen dollars plus eight dollars a gigabyte. When do they cost the same? To find out, you need x on both sides of an equation.
scenes.caption: Plan A costs $30 plus $5 per GB. Plan B costs $18 plus $8 per GB. When do they cost the same? To find out, you need x on both sides of an equation.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Take 3 boxes off EACH pan and the scales stay level
scenes.science: Subtract 3x from both sides to get x on one side
scenes.breaks: you can't remove negative boxes from real scales, but algebra handles negative terms easily.
scenes.say: Picture scales with seven boxes on the left, and three boxes plus some weights on the right. Take three boxes off each side. Still balanced, and now boxes are only on the left. That's how you move x to one side.

scenes.heading: The order of attack
scenes.say: Here is the order. Expand any brackets. Collect like terms on each side. Move the x terms to one side, usually by subtracting the smaller one. Then solve and check both sides.

scenes.heading: x on both sides
scenes.question: Solve 2x + 9 = 5x − 3.
scenes.say: Solve two x plus nine equals five x minus three. Subtract the smaller x term, two x, from both sides: nine equals three x minus three. Add three: twelve equals three x. Divide by three: x equals four.
scenes.caption: Solve 2x + 9 = 5x − 3. Subtract the smaller x-term, 2x, from both sides: 9 = 3x − 3. Add 3: 12 = 3x. Divide by 3: x = 4.

scenes.heading: Brackets first
scenes.question: Solve 3(2x − 1) = 2(x + 7) + 1.
scenes.say: Expand both brackets: six x minus three equals two x plus fourteen plus one. Tidy up: two x plus fifteen. Subtract two x: four x minus three equals fifteen. Add three: four x equals eighteen. So x equals four point five.
scenes.caption: Expand both brackets: 6x − 3 = 2x + 14 + 1. Tidy up: 2x + 15. Subtract 2x: 4x − 3 = 15. Add 3: 4x = 18. So x = 4.5.

scenes.heading: Fractions on both sides
scenes.question: Solve (x + 3)/2 = (2x − 1)/3.
scenes.say: Multiply both sides by six, the lowest common denominator: three lots of x plus three equals two lots of two x minus one. Expand: three x plus nine equals four x minus two. Subtract three x, then add two: x equals eleven.
scenes.caption: Multiply both sides by 6, the lowest common denominator: 3(x + 3) = 2(2x − 1). Expand: 3x + 9 = 4x − 2. Subtract 3x, then add 2: x = 11.

scenes.heading: When x disappears
scenes.say: Sometimes the x terms cancel. Two lots of x plus three equals two x plus six is true for every x. But two lots of x plus three equals two x plus five leaves six equals five, which is never true. No solution.

points: Multiply EVERY term by the LCD
Check both sides give the same
scenes.say: Quick recap. Expand brackets first. Subtract the smaller x term from both sides. Multiply every term by the lowest common denominator. Then check both sides. Now try the practice questions!
